It is a Procumbens Nana. The previous owner had it in full sun. I now have it in a position on my porch where it receives a few hours of morning sun and the rest of the day it is shaded. I have not trimmed it yet because I wanted to get an idea of what to do first. Any help is appreciated.

I'm not great with potted plants, but have attended some talks on dwarf conifers...and know some of the pruning tips on full sized ones. So I figured I'd look around online, and there seems to be a lot of advice on this particular tree.

Basic care is well documented...like on this site. . I didn't realise that the juniper you have is best suited as an outdoor plant (taking winter care into account depending in where you live). I think you are doing well to protect it from full sun all day...I've burnt some tender cypresses in planters by leaving them too exposed. Make sure your pot has good drainage too. They don't like to dry out completely, but they also don't like to sit in wet mushy soil.

This site has good information on how the trees circulatory system (so to speak). Parts of the tree can look dead, and the rest of the tree can be quite healthy. If I were you, I'd probably trim off the dead bits to the trunk, then wait a while before starting to shape the remaining tree. Let it catch it's breath before it has to start more new growth.

And finally...this site explains how to do the actual trimming.

One time I did try a bonsai, I remember that the stones on top were kind of glued together and stuck on top. Made it weird for air and water access. If yours is like that, you might want to break those stones up.
